originality.rationale: The mean-square amplification cubic for the Gaussian two-point law is implied by a published two-point randomized-theta theorem and is excluded as a standalone novelty claim. The accepted statement is the sharp all-Borel-law moment-constrained optimizer transition r_c, its converse via a feasible three-atom measure, and unique optimal radius, absent from the inspected principal paper and published two-point theorem. Classical Gaussian quadrature extremality provides a technique but not this rational-objective sign transition. Publication priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: A general moment-problem principal-representation theorem or earlier stability-design result could encode the sharp rational-objective optimizer under different terminology.
The classical Gaussian quadrature contact technique itself is not new; the value and originality depend on the exact positive crossover and its constructive converse.
The comparison with Trefethen (2022) relies on an abstract rather than full text, and no conclusion about its complete contents is asserted.

value.rationale: Three-moment calibration is a natural statistical constraint corresponding to uniform stage sampling and the exact two-node Gaussian quadrature moments. The result classifies when Gaussian stages are globally optimal even against arbitrary-support distributions, gives a sharp positive optimizer transition verified in both directions, and yields a quantitatively improved sharp mean-square stability interval. It is a mathematical stability-design principle rather than a routine sampled parameter case; no broad nonlinear significance is claimed.
